summary: Sound, well-attributed launch fusion on shapes where this problem is launch-heavy (bs=1 is 55 us with 7.8 us in the three replaced kernels). Run it alone with sharper self-check logging. No companion is needed because the in-run bs=128/256 controls, the per-kernel profile rows and the unheld align-remote-sentinel-ids probe between them separate the possible mechanisms.
justification: The mechanism is plausible and measured, not assumed. In bacd1f502f4e46fa the kernels being replaced cost: bs=1 index 1.8 + unrolled 1.6 + small_batch_align 4.4 us (7.8 of 52.0 us summed kernel time, 55.3 us median); bs=8 1.7+1.6+4.9; bs=16 2.2+1.4+5.6; bs=32 2.4+1.9+6.5. The same _align_small_kernel measured 4.3 us at T=32 on decode_layer (0a0af8669ffe4cb0) and passed its 60-case self-check. Net savings are therefore about 6.5 us at bs=32 (~3%, above that shape's ~1.4% err) and probably 5-6 us at bs=1 (~9-10%). Shapes and directions agree with TASK.md: six equal-weight (60) loads, bs<=32 changed and bs=128/256 untouched as controls. A ~10% gain on decode_1 plus 3-4% on verify_1, decode_16 and decode_32 is roughly +2.5-3% on the geomean, about the size of the CI, so judge it per shape. The unrolled_elementwise row is very probably not from the moe_align_block_size wrapper, contrary to the hypothesis. In align-single-token-ep (a7bb0cecaf8d4de1) the align was replaced but a 1.2 us unrolled_elementwise call remained. It most likely comes from PyTorch advanced indexing casting the int32 index to int64 for expert_map[local_ids], and it scales with M (3.2 us at bs=128) like the gather does. Either way it is removed, because the gather goes away. Weakest link: the new kernel's own latency at small T. It is a single program doing a [BLOCK_N,32] one-hot cumsum plus a [MB_BLOCK,32] segment test, and only its T=32 time (4.3 us) is known. If it runs ~4 us even at T=1-8 (fixed cost of the cumsum and reductions on one SM), bs=1 gains ~3.5 us (6%), not 5-6. LESSONS also records that launch fusion was flat on larger layer shapes. Here, though, the shapes are 55-207 us and the replaced kernels are 4-14% of them, so this is the case LESSONS says pays.
confounders: sglang-marlin-path-parity: it sets the 32-expert moe_align_block_size this replaces, and with it how remote (-1) routes are handled. If SGLang's small-batch kernel at num_experts=32 buckets -1 routes into phantom m-blocks (the open question align-remote-sentinel-ids exists to probe), the Triton kernel drops them. Marlin then sees a smaller n_padded and fewer m-blocks, and part of any gain is Marlin work removed, not launches removed. The decode self-check would not catch this: it compares n_pad only against SGLang's local-expert blocks and never against SGLang's own r_pad. Remedy without a companion: in the port's self-check, print per case whether n_pad != r_pad (as info), and read the Marlin row against the sentinel probe.

post-expert-norm-triton-small-m: no timing confound. It consumes local_ids (skipping -1) at M<32, and SGLang's fused sum consumes slot_expert_ids at bs=32. The new kernel must reproduce local_ids bit-exactly in dtype int32, shape [M,8], contiguous. If it does not, the failure is a correctness failure on the bs=1/4/33 tests, not a silent speed artifact. Its gain does not change what this hypothesis removes.
interference: No companion is warranted. A gain or loss is attributable from one run. (1) bs=128/256 keep master's exact path, so they measure drift. (2) The profile shows the replaced rows (index_elementwise, unrolled_elementwise, small_batch_expert_kernel) disappear and _align_small_kernel appears with its own time, and Triton times reproduce within ~1% (LESSONS). (3) The only plausible second mechanism is a change in Marlin's m-block count if master's align buckets -1 routes. The self-check can settle that deterministically and for free in prepare() by logging n_pad vs SGLang's r_pad, and the now-unheld align-remote-sentinel-ids measures its timing effect on master. An ab-revert of either landed hypothesis would not make the result clearer: parity defines the path being replaced, and the post-norm kernel is downstream and indifferent. A capacity control like the one on decode_layer is not needed, because master already allocates the 32-expert capacity M*8+32*(bsm-1), which the port keeps.
rules_flags: None blocking. The branch is on num_tokens (shape) only. There is no host sync in kernel_fn, and the buffers are torch.empty sized from M and bsm. Warm-compile and self-check run in prepare() on synthetic ids only; .tolist()/.item() appear only there.

Pass local_start/local_count as the bank's own prepare-time values (or constexpr / do_not_specialize) and warm-compile with the same values. Triton int specialization must not leave a variant that first JIT-compiles inside the warmup or graph-capture path.
Prefer passing data['topk_ids'] directly and casting in-kernel (tl.load(...).to(tl.int32)), as the decode kernel does. This keeps the path free of any host-side dtype copy.
open_questions: Does SGLang's moe_align_block_size(local_ids, bsm, 32) put the -1 routes into any m-block? Log r_pad vs n_pad per self-check case. If they differ, part of the gain is Marlin work, and the align-remote-sentinel-ids result should be read alongside this one.
What is _align_small_kernel's own time at T=1, 8 and 16? It is known only at T=32 (4.3 us). Report it from the profile together with the absence of the three replaced rows.

If unrolled_elementwise survives at bs<=32, record where it comes from. The evidence (it survived align-single-token-ep) suggests the int64 index cast in expert_map[...], which this change removes. A survivor would point to silu_and_mul or the Marlin wrapper.

Within-expert route order differed from SGLang's at T=16 and T=32 on decode (info only). Confirm the Marlin outputs are row-independent so per-row results are bit-identical; correctness should be unaffected.
